To learn more about this opportunity, please go to the NYS Grants Gateway at the following web address:
https://grantsgateway.ny.gov/Intelligrants_NYSGG/module/nysgg/gggrantmodule.aspx
Applications must be submitted online via the Grants Gateway by the date and time posted on the cover of this RFA.  Reference materials and videos are available for Grantees applying to funding opportunities on the NYS Grants Gateway.  Please visit the Grants Management website at the following web address:
https://grantsmanagement.ny.gov/
and select the “Apply for a Grant” from the Apply & Manage menu. There is also a more detailed “Grants Gateway: Vendor User Guide” available in the documents section under Training & Guidance; For Grant Applicants on this page as well.  Training webinars are also provided by the Grants Gateway Team.  Dates and times for webinar instruction can be located at the following web address:
https://grantsmanagement.ny.gov/live-webinars
.
To apply for this opportunity:
Log into the
Grants Gateway
as either a "Grantee" or "Grantee Contract Signatory".
On the Grants Gateway home page, click the "View Opportunities" button.
Use the search fields to locate an opportunity; search by State agency (DOH) or enter the Grant Opportunity name
.
Click on “Search” button to initiate the search.
Click on the name of the Grant Opportunity from the search results grid and then select the “APPLY FOR GRANT OPPORTUNITY” button located bottom left of the Main page of the Grant Opportunity.
Once the application is complete, prospective grantees are
strongly encouraged
to submit their applications at least 48 hours prior to the due date and time.  This will allow sufficient opportunity for the applicant to obtain assistance and take corrective action should there be a technical issue with the submission process.  Both DOH and Grants Management staff are available to answer applicant’s technical questions and provide technical assistance prior to the application due date and time.  Contact information for the Grants Management Team is available under Section IV. B. of this RFA.
PLEASE NOTE:
Although DOH and the Grants Management staff will do their best to address concerns that are identified less than 48 hours prior to the due date and time, there is no guarantee that they will be resolved in time for the application to be submitted and, therefore, considered for funding.
The Grants Gateway will always notify applicants of successful submission.  If a prospective grantee does not get a successful submission message assigning their application a unique ID number, it has not successfully submitted an application.  During the application process, please pay particular attention to the following:
Not-for-profit applicants must be prequalified on the due date for this application submission.  Be sure to maintain prequalification status between funding opportunities.  Three of a not-for-profit’s essential financial documents - the IRS990, Financial Statement and Charities Bureau filing - expire on an annual basis.  If these documents are allowed to expire, the not-for-profit’s prequalification status expires as well, and it will not be eligible for State grant funding until its documentation is updated and approved, and prequalified status is reinstated.
Only individuals with the roles “Grantee Contract Signatory” or “Grantee System Administrator” can submit an application.
Prior to submission, the system will automatically initiate a global error checking process to protect against incomplete applications.  An applicant may need to attend to certain parts of the application prior to being able to submit the application successfully.  You can also run the global error check at any time in the application process. (see p.68 of the Grants Gateway: Vendor User Guide).
Grantees should use numbers, letters and underscores when naming their uploaded files. There cannot be any special characters in the uploaded file name.  Also, be aware of the restriction on file size (10 MB) when uploading documents.

grants.title: Statewide Health Care Facility Transformation Program IV – Residential and Community-based Alternatives to the Traditional Model of Nursing Home Care
grants.summary: This grant funds projects that support residential and community-based alternatives to traditional nursing home care in New York State.
grants.description: The Statewide Health Care Facility Transformation Program IV aims to provide funding for projects that develop residential and community-based alternatives to traditional nursing home care. The program is issued by the New York State Department of Health, Office of Aging and Long Term Care. Eligible applicants must submit their applications through the NYS Grants Gateway system. Not-for-profit applicants must maintain prequalification status to be eligible. Applications are encouraged to be submitted at least 48 hours before the deadline to address any technical issues.
grants.eligibility_notes: Eligible applicants include organizations that can develop residential and community-based alternatives to traditional nursing home care. Not-for-profit organizations must be prequalified.
key_requirements: Applications must be submitted through the NYS Grants Gateway system.
Not-for-profit applicants must maintain prequalification status.
Applications must be submitted by 4 p.m. ET on the deadline date.
Applicants are encouraged to submit applications at least 48 hours before the deadline.

grants.title: Statewide Health Care Facility Transformation Program IV and V Health Information Technology, Cybersecurity, and Telehealth Transformation
grants.summary: This grant funds projects to improve health information technology, cybersecurity, and telehealth capabilities in healthcare facilities across New York State.
grants.description: The Statewide Health Care Facility Transformation Program IV and V aims to support healthcare facilities in New York State by funding projects that enhance health information technology, cybersecurity, and telehealth infrastructure. The program is designed to improve the quality of care, patient safety, and operational efficiency. Eligible applicants include healthcare facilities and organizations that meet the program's requirements. Applications must be submitted online via the NYS Grants Gateway. Prequalification is required for not-for-profit applicants.
grants.eligibility_notes: Eligible applicants include healthcare facilities and organizations that meet the program's requirements. Not-for-profit applicants must be prequalified.
key_requirements: Applications must be submitted online via the NYS Grants Gateway.
Not-for-profit applicants must be prequalified.
Applicants must adhere to file naming and size restrictions.
Applications must be submitted by individuals with the appropriate roles in the Grants Gateway system.

grants.summary: This grant funds housing subsidies and rapid transition housing for eligible individuals in New York State.
grants.description: The Olmstead Housing Subsidy/Rapid Transition Housing Program provides funding to support housing subsidies and rapid transition housing for individuals in need within New York State. The program is issued by the New York State Department of Health, Office of Health Insurance Programs, Division of Program Development and Management. Applications must be submitted online via the NYS Grants Gateway. Not-for-profit applicants must be prequalified to apply. Technical assistance is available for applicants during the submission process.
grants.eligibility_notes: Not-for-profit organizations that are prequalified on the due date are eligible to apply.
key_requirements: Applicants must be not-for-profit organizations.
Applicants must be prequalified on the due date.
Applications must be submitted online via the NYS Grants Gateway.

strongly encouraged

Applications must be submitted online via the Grants Gateway by the date and time posted on the cover of this RFA.  Reference materials and videos are available for Grantees applying to funding opportunities on the NYS Grants Gateway.  Please visit the Grants Management website at the following web address:
https://grantsmanagement.ny.gov/
and select the “Apply for a Grant” from the Apply & Manage menu. There is also a more detailed “Grants Gateway: Vendor User Guide” available in the documents section under Training & Guidance; For Grant Applicants on this page as well.  Training webinars are also provided by the Grants Gateway Team.  Dates and times for webinar instruction can be located at the following web address:
https://grantsmanagement.ny.gov/live-webinars
.
To apply for this opportunity:
Log into the
Grants Gateway
as either a "Grantee" or "Grantee Contract Signatory".
On the Grants Gateway home page, click the "View Opportunities" button.
Use the search fields to locate an opportunity; search by State agency (DOH) or enter the Grant Opportunity name
.
Click on “Search” button to initiate the search.
Click on the name of the Grant Opportunity from the search results grid and then select the “APPLY FOR GRANT OPPORTUNITY” button located bottom left of the Main page of the Grant Opportunity.
Once the application is complete, prospective grantees are
strongly encouraged
to submit their applications at least 48 hours prior to the due date and time.  This will allow sufficient opportunity for the applicant to obtain assistance and take corrective action should there be a technical issue with the submission process.  Both DOH and Grants Management staff are available to answer applicant’s technical questions and provide technical assistance prior to the application due date and time.  Contact information for the Grants Management Team is available under Section IV. B. of this RFA.
PLEASE NOTE:
Although DOH and the Grants Management staff will do their best to address concerns that are identified less than 48 hours prior to the due date and time, there is no guarantee that they will be resolved in time for the application to be submitted and, therefore, considered for funding.
The Grants Gateway will always notify applicants of successful submission.  If a prospective grantee does not get a successful submission message assigning their application a unique ID number, it has not successfully submitted an application.  During the application process, please pay particular attention to the following:
Not-for-profit applicants must be prequalified on the due date for this application submission.  Be sure to maintain prequalification status between funding opportunities.  Three of a not-for-profit’s essential financial documents - the IRS990, Financial Statement and Charities Bureau filing - expire on an annual basis.  If these documents are allowed to expire, the not-for-profit’s prequalification status expires as well, and it will not be eligible for State grant funding until its documentation is updated and approved, and prequalified status is reinstated.
Only individuals with the roles “Grantee Contract Signatory” or “Grantee System Administrator” can submit an application.
Prior to submission, the system will automatically initiate a global error checking process to protect against incomplete applications.  An applicant may need to attend to certain parts of the application prior to being able to submit the application successfully.  You can also run the global error check at any time in the application process. (see p.68 of the Grants Gateway: Vendor User Guide).
Grantees should use numbers, letters and underscores when naming their uploaded files. There cannot be any special characters in the uploaded file name.  Also, be aware of the restriction on file size (10 MB) when uploading documents.

The program will benefit coroners and the communities they serve by improving the quality of death investigations. Applications must be submitted online via the NYS Grants Gateway. Not-for-profit applicants must be prequalified, and all required documents must be up to date. Technical assistance is available for applicants during the submission process.

Applicants must be prequalified in the NYS Grants Gateway system.
Applications must be submitted online via the Grants Gateway.

grants.summary: This grant funds programs aimed at expanding harm reduction services for priority populations who use drugs in New York State.
grants.description: The grant seeks to support organizations in New York State to expand harm reduction services for priority populations who use drugs. The purpose is to reduce drug-related harm and improve health outcomes for these populations. Eligible applicants must submit their applications through the NYS Grants Gateway system. Not-for-profit organizations must maintain prequalification status to be eligible. Applications must be submitted by the specified deadline, and technical assistance is available for applicants.
grants.eligibility_notes: Eligible applicants include organizations in New York State, particularly not-for-profits that are prequalified in the NYS Grants Gateway system.
key_requirements: Applicants must be organizations based in New York State.
Not-for-profit applicants must be prequalified in the NYS Grants Gateway system.
Applications must be submitted online via the Grants Gateway system.
Applicants must adhere to the submission deadline of October 3, 2023, by 4:00 PM ET.

grants.summary: This grant funds mentorship programs aimed at supporting individuals in medicine and other healthcare professions.
grants.description: The Mentorship in Medicine and Other Healthcare Professions grant, offered by the New York State Department of Health, aims to support mentorship programs that promote diversity and inclusion in healthcare professions. The grant is managed by the Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities Prevention. Eligible applicants must submit their applications online via the Grants Gateway system. Not-for-profit organizations must maintain prequalification status to be eligible. Technical assistance is available for applicants during the submission process.

key_requirements: Applicants must be not-for-profit organizations.
Organizations must maintain prequalification status.
Applications must be submitted online via the Grants Gateway system.

There is also a more detailed “Grants Gateway: Vendor User Guide” available in the documents section under Training & Guidance; For Grant Applicants on this page as well. .
To apply for this opportunity:
Log into the
Grants Gateway
as either a "Grantee" or "Grantee Contract Signatory".
On the Grants Gateway home page, click the "View Opportunities" button.
Use the search fields to locate an opportunity; search by State agency (DOH) or enter the Grant Opportunity name
.
Click on “Search” button to initiate the search.
Click on the name of the Grant Opportunity from the search results grid and then select the “APPLY FOR GRANT OPPORTUNITY” button located bottom left of the Main page of the Grant Opportunity.
Once the application is complete, prospective grantees are
strongly encouraged
to submit their applications at least 48 hours prior to the due date and time.  This will allow sufficient opportunity for the applicant to obtain assistance and take corrective action should there be a technical issue with the submission process.  Both DOH and Grants Management staff are available to answer applicant’s technical questions and provide technical assistance prior to the application due date and time.  Contact information for the Grants Management Team is available under Section IV. B. of this RFA.
PLEASE NOTE:
Although DOH and the Grants Management staff will do their best to address concerns that are identified less than 48 hours prior to the due date and time, there is no guarantee that they will be resolved in time for the application to be submitted and, therefore, considered for funding.
The Grants Gateway will always notify applicants of successful submission.  If a prospective grantee does not get a successful submission message assigning their application a unique ID number, it has not successfully submitted an application.  During the application process, please pay particular attention to the following:
Not-for-profit applicants must be prequalified on the due date for this application submission.  Be sure to maintain prequalification status between funding opportunities.  Three of a not-for-profit’s essential financial documents - the IRS990, Financial Statement and Charities Bureau filing - expire on an annual basis.  If these documents are allowed to expire, the not-for-profit’s prequalification status expires as well, and it will not be eligible for State grant funding until its documentation is updated and approved, and prequalified status is reinstated.
Only individuals with the roles “Grantee Contract Signatory” or “Grantee System Administrator” can submit an application.
Prior to submission, the system will automatically initiate a global error checking process to protect against incomplete applications.  An applicant may need to attend to certain parts of the application prior to being able to submit the application successfully.  You can also run the global error check at any time in the application process. (see p.68 of the Grants Gateway: Vendor User Guide).
Grantees should use numbers, letters and underscores when naming their uploaded files. There cannot be any special characters in the uploaded file name.  Also, be aware of the restriction on file size (10 MB) when uploading documents.

The purpose is to improve understanding and treatment of spinal cord injuries, benefiting patients and the medical community. Applications must be submitted online via the Grants Gateway system. Not-for-profit applicants must maintain prequalification status to be eligible.

key_requirements: Applicants must submit via Grants Gateway.
Not-for-profit organizations must be prequalified.
Applications must be complete and error-checked before submission.
Uploaded files must adhere to naming conventions and size restrictions.

Not-for-profit organizations must maintain prequalification status to be eligible. Applications must be submitted online by the specified deadline.

Not-for-profit applicants must be prequalified on the due date for application submission.
Applicants must maintain prequalification status between funding opportunities.

To learn more about this opportunity, please go to the NYS Grants Gateway at the following web address:
https://grantsgateway.ny.gov/Intelligrants_NYSGG/module/nysgg/gggrantmodule.aspx
Applications must be submitted online via the Grants Gateway by the date and time posted on the cover of this RFA.  Reference materials and videos are available for Grantees applying to funding opportunities on the NYS Grants Gateway.  Please visit the Grants Management website at the following web address:
https://grantsmanagement.ny.gov/
and select the “Apply for a Grant” from the Apply & Manage menu. There is also a more detailed “Grants Gateway: Vendor User Guide” available in the documents section under Training & Guidance; For Grant Applicants on this page as well.  Training webinars are also provided by the Grants Gateway Team.  Dates and times for webinar instruction can be located at the following web address:
https://grantsmanagement.ny.gov/live-webinars
.
To apply for this opportunity:
Log into the
Grants Gateway
as either a "Grantee" or "Grantee Contract Signatory".
On the Grants Gateway home page, click the "View Opportunities" button.
Use the search fields to locate an opportunity; search by State agency (DOH) or enter the Grant Opportunity name
.
Click on “Search” button to initiate the search.
Click on the name of the Grant Opportunity from the search results grid and then select the “APPLY FOR GRANT OPPORTUNITY” button located bottom left of the Main page of the Grant Opportunity.
Once the application is complete, prospective grantees are
strongly encouraged
to submit their applications at least 48 hours prior to the due date and time.  This will allow sufficient opportunity for the applicant to obtain assistance and take corrective action should there be a technical issue with the submission process.  Both DOH and Grants Management staff are available to answer applicant’s technical questions and provide technical assistance prior to the application due date and time.  Contact information for the Grants Management Team is available under Section IV. B. of this RFA.
PLEASE NOTE:
Although DOH and the Grants Management staff will do their best to address concerns that are identified less than 48 hours prior to the due date and time, there is no guarantee that they will be resolved in time for the application to be submitted and, therefore, considered for funding.
The Grants Gateway will always notify applicants of successful submission.  If a prospective grantee does not get a successful submission message assigning their application a unique ID number, it has not successfully submitted an application.  During the application process, please pay particular attention to the following:
Not-for-profit applicants must be prequalified on the due date for this application submission.  Be sure to maintain prequalification status between funding opportunities.  Three of a not-for-profit’s essential financial documents - the IRS990, Financial Statement and Charities Bureau filing - expire on an annual basis.  If these documents are allowed to expire, the not-for-profit’s prequalification status expires as well, and it will not be eligible for State grant funding until its documentation is updated and approved, and prequalified status is reinstated.
Only individuals with the roles “Grantee Contract Signatory” or “Grantee System Administrator” can submit an application.
Prior to submission, the system will automatically initiate a global error checking process to protect against incomplete applications.  An applicant may need to attend to certain parts of the application prior to being able to submit the application successfully.  You can also run the global error check at any time in the application process. (see p.68 of the Grants Gateway: Vendor User Guide).
Grantees should use numbers, letters and underscores when naming their uploaded files. There cannot be any special characters in the uploaded file name.  Also, be aware of the restriction on file size (10 MB) when uploading documents.

To apply for this opportunity:
Log into the
Grants Gateway
as either a "Grantee" or "Grantee Contract Signatory".
On the Grants Gateway home page, click the "View Opportunities" button.
Use the search fields to locate an opportunity; search by State agency (DOH) or enter the Grant Opportunity name
.
Click on “Search” button to initiate the search.
Click on the name of the Grant Opportunity from the search results grid and then select the “APPLY FOR GRANT OPPORTUNITY” button located bottom left of the Main page of the Grant Opportunity.
Once the application is complete, prospective grantees are
strongly encouraged
to submit their applications at least 48 hours prior to the due date and time.  This will allow sufficient opportunity for the applicant to obtain assistance and take corrective action should there be a technical issue with the submission process.  Both DOH and Grants Management staff are available to answer applicant’s technical questions and provide technical assistance prior to the application due date and time.  Contact information for the Grants Management Team is available under Section IV. B. of this RFA.
PLEASE NOTE:
Although DOH and the Grants Management staff will do their best to address concerns that are identified less than 48 hours prior to the due date and time, there is no guarantee that they will be resolved in time for the application to be submitted and, therefore, considered for funding.
The Grants Gateway will always notify applicants of successful submission.  If a prospective grantee does not get a successful submission message assigning their application a unique ID number, it has not successfully submitted an application.  During the application process, please pay particular attention to the following:
Not-for-profit applicants must be prequalified on the due date for this application submission.  Be sure to maintain prequalification status between funding opportunities.  Three of a not-for-profit’s essential financial documents - the IRS990, Financial Statement and Charities Bureau filing - expire on an annual basis.  If these documents are allowed to expire, the not-for-profit’s prequalification status expires as well, and it will not be eligible for State grant funding until its documentation is updated and approved, and prequalified status is reinstated.
Only individuals with the roles “Grantee Contract Signatory” or “Grantee System Administrator” can submit an application.
Prior to submission, the system will automatically initiate a global error checking process to protect against incomplete applications.  An applicant may need to attend to certain parts of the application prior to being able to submit the application successfully.  You can also run the global error check at any time in the application process. (see p.68 of the Grants Gateway: Vendor User Guide).
Grantees should use numbers, letters and underscores when naming their uploaded files. There cannot be any special characters in the uploaded file name.  Also, be aware of the restriction on file size (10 MB) when uploading documents.

grants.title: RFA #20171 – Drinking Water Fluoridation – Rolling Submissions
grants.summary: This grant funds planning, feasibility, implementation, and maintenance projects for drinking water fluoridation in New York State municipalities.
grants.description: The grant aims to support municipalities in New York State to improve public health through drinking water fluoridation. Funding is available for planning and feasibility studies (Component A) as well as implementation and maintenance projects (Component B). Applications must be submitted via email with required documentation, including budget details and technical submittals. Eligible municipalities can apply by following the updated submission guidelines.
grants.award_text: $50,000 or more for Component B projects
grants.eligibility_notes: Eligible municipalities in New York State can apply.
key_requirements: Must be a municipality in New York State
Submit all required documentation in one PDF file
Budget document must be submitted as an Excel file
Applications must be emailed to DFHDWF@health.ny.gov
Projects must expand or create new activities, not supplant existing ones

 I. Introduction 
 
The New York State Department of  Health (NYSDOH), Divi sion of Family Health (DFH), Bureau of 
Child Health (BCH) announces the availability of  funding through this Reque st for Applications 
(RFA) to maintain and expand New York State (NYS) residents’ access to optim ally fluoridated water. 
The purpose of this RFA is to identify eligible NY S municipalities that want to work with NYS to 
increase the number of communities with access to fluoridated water. The key characteristic of a 
successful applicant is the ability  to document a proposed NYS muni cipal drinking water fluoridation 
project utilizing the documents provided. There are two components available in this funding 
opportunity. Component A is for elig ible municipalities seeking to de velop an Engineering Report to 
determine the feasibility of starting community water fluoridation or upgrade/modify an existing 
fluoridation system. Component B is  for eligible municipalities looki ng to purchase, upgrade, replace 
or repair water fluoridation equipment* to init iate or maintain community water fluoridation. 
 
II. Who May Apply  
 
All eligible municipalities must  include Attachment 1 – Application Cover Page  for Component A 
and B.  
 
An eligible municipality  for either component must  be a: 
 NYS county, city, town, village, or public aut hority (municipality) that owns both its public 
water system and the water supply for the system; AND  
 Community water system* or sell water wholesale*  to one or more comm unity water systems. 
A Component A  eligible municipality must also meet ONE  of the following criteria: 
 Serve at least 5,000 people (incl udes people served dire ctly through service connections* and/or 
indirectly through wholesale* purchase); OR, 
 Currently be fluoridating the public water supply; OR, 
 Have the necessary approvals in place to fluor idate the public water supply in accordance with 
New York State Public Health Law §1100-a. (Click on Laws at top bar; choose Laws of New 
York; scroll down to PHL – Public Health Law; enter 1100-a in search box and click “Search”.) 
 AND must  include Attachment 2  – Component A Technical Submittal. 
A Component B  eligible municipality must also meet ONE  of the following criteria: 
 Currently be fluoridating the public water supply; OR, 
 Have the necessary approvals in place to fluor idate the public water supply in accordance with 
New York State Public Health Law §1100-a. (Click on Laws at top bar; choose Laws of New 
York; scroll down to PHL – Public Health Law; enter 1100-a in search box and click “Search”.) 
 AND must  include Attachment 3  – Componenet B Technical S ubmittal for Propsals $50,000 or 
Less OR Attachment 4  – Component B Technical Submittal  for Projects $50,001 or More OR 
Projects Initiative Fluoridation. 
Please Note: Federal Government, Native American, private, and state-owned water systems are not 
eligible for this funding.  
Terms marked with *asterisk are further defined in Attachment 5  - Definitions Document . 
Eligible Municipalities w ill need to submit a separate applicatio n for each project and component.

 Eligible Municipalities can only submit an ap plication for one Component (either Component A 
or B) of this RFA at a time. If both Components are required for a municipality’s project, it is 
advised that the eligible municipality submit an application for Component A (Planning and 
Feasibility Projects) first. Once a successful eligible municipal ity has completed its Component A 
project (Engineering Repor t developed and final voucher and pr ogress report submitted to NYSDOH), 
an eligible municipality may then submit a separa te application for Component B (Implementation and 
Maintenance Projects). 
Submitted projects determined to not meet the requirements will be encouraged to resubmit again. 
 A. Available Funding 
 
The total funding available is $2.5 million annually. As stated in the Term of Contract (Section G), 24-
month term, with a start date approximately  six months from aw ard letter date.  
Component A applicants may request up to $50,000 for the full contract term. Total funding for 
Component A is projected to be  $500,000 annually for all awards.  
Component B applicants may requ est up to $1 million for the full contract term. Total funding for 
Component B is projected to be $2 million annually fo r all awards.  
Note:  If for any reason the applications  for either component do not full y utilize the allocated funding, 
the Department reserves the ri ght to reallocate sa vings from one component to another.  
Please Note: To ensure that projects will be  completed within the 24-month contract period, 
municipalities should consult with their local or NYSDOH  and initiate and/or obtain the necessary 
endorsements or approvals for their project sc ope/engineering report pr ior to submitting an 
application. 
This funding is for “new” projects  only, meaning any previously comp leted work, such as fluoridation 
system remodel in 2020, or work curr ently in progress, such as an E ngineering Report in development, 
is not eligible for reimbursemen t under this RFA. In addition, f unding may not be used to supplant 
funds for existing staff or ot her fluoridation activities. 
If funding becomes limited for any reason during the 6- year period of this RFA,  the project will be 
suspended with adequate notice in the NYS Contract Reporter.

Attachment 5: Definitions  
 1. Community water system: A public water system which serves at least five service 
connections used by year -round residents or regularly serves at least 25 year -round 
residents.  
2. Service connection:  The pertinent pipes, valves , and fittings that connect a distribution 
system to a consumer’s facility.  
3. Water fluoridation equipment:  The equipment required for the fluoride feed system 
(saturator, dry feed, or acid -based system), testing and analysis of fluoride, and/or 
personal operator safety when operating the fluoride feed system.  
4. Wholesale:  A public water system that treats source water as necessary to produce 
finished water and then delivers some or all of that finished water to another public water 
system. Delivery may be through a direct connection or through the distribution system of one or more consecutive systems.

QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS  
1. Question: What is the definition of an eligible municipality?    Does the County fall under that category as an 
oversight agency?  We do not operate any water facilities but would apply for the planning portion to look 
at feasibility.  
 
Response: The term “municipality” shall mean a county, city, town or village. To qualify for this funding opportunity, as noted in Section II of the RFA,  “An eligible municipality for either component must be a: 
• NYS county, city, town, village, or public authority (municipality) that owns both its public 
water system and the water supply for the system; AND 
• Community water system* or sell water wholesale* to one or more community water systems.”  
 
For more information regarding the feasibility of ownership of a public water system and/or supply for the system, please contact the New York State Department of Health’s Bureau of Water Supply Protection at bpwsp@health.ny.gov  
 
2. Question: Have the necessary approvals in place to fluoridate the public water supply in accordance with PHL 1100- a.  I’ve reviewed the law and it’s not exactly clear what approvals are needed.  Does it mean that 
the municipality has to pass a law approving fluoridation or funds for fluoridation?  In my opinion most municipalities will not pass a law until they know it is feasible.  
Response: For more information regarding the necessary approvals in place to fluoridate the public water supply in accordance with PHL 1100-a , please contact the New York State Department of 
Health’s Bureau of Water Supply Protection at bpwsp@health.ny.gov. 
 
3. Question: Am I reading below notice properly that the fluoridation program has no deadline and submissions can be made at any time up until 9/28/28? 
 
Response: Yes.  As noted in Section V.A. [Application Format/Content], “Applications must be submitted via the Grants Gateway by the Application deadline date and time specified on the Cover Page of this RFA.”  The Cover Page of the RFA indicates “Applications Due: Rolling Submissions until September 28, 2028”.  
 
4. Question: I am interested in learning more about the above RFA, and I was wondering if you are able to send Attachment 2 (Component A Technical Submittal) for me to review. I have not been able to find this portion of the RFA in the Grants Gateway system.

Drinking Water Fluoridation RFA – Rolling Submissions 
3 
 I. Introduction 
 
The New York State Department of  Health (NYSDOH), Divi sion of Family Health (DFH), Bureau of 
Child Health (BCH) announces the availability of  funding through this Reque st for Applications 
(RFA) to maintain and expand New York State (NYS) residents’ access to optim ally fluoridated water. 
The purpose of this RFA is to identify eligible NY S municipalities that want to work with NYS to 
increase the number of communities with access to fluoridated water. The key characteristic of a 
successful applicant is the ability  to document a proposed NYS muni cipal drinking water fluoridation 
project utilizing the documents provided. There are two components available in this funding 
opportunity. Component A is for elig ible municipalities seeking to de velop an Engineering Report to 
determine the feasibility of starting community water fluoridation or upgrade/modify an existing 
fluoridation system. Component B is  for eligible municipalities looki ng to purchase, upgrade, replace 
or repair water fluoridation equipment* to init iate or maintain community water fluoridation. 
 
II. Who May Apply  
 
All eligible municipalities must  include Attachment 1 – Application Cover Page  for Component A 
and B.  
 
An eligible municipality  for either component must  be a: 
 NYS county, city, town, village, or public aut hority (municipality) that owns both its public 
water system and the water supply for the system; AND  
 Community water system* or sell water wholesale*  to one or more comm unity water systems. 
A Component A  eligible municipality must also meet ONE  of the following criteria: 
 Serve at least 5,000 people (incl udes people served dire ctly through service connections* and/or 
indirectly through wholesale* purchase); OR, 
 Currently be fluoridating the public water supply; OR, 
 Have the necessary approvals in place to fluor idate the public water supply in accordance with 
New York State Public Health Law §1100-a. (Click on Laws at top bar; choose Laws of New 
York; scroll down to PHL – Public Health Law; enter 1100-a in search box and click “Search”.) 
 AND must  include Attachment 2  – Component A Technical Submittal. 
A Component B  eligible municipality must also meet ONE  of the following criteria: 
 Currently be fluoridating the public water supply; OR, 
 Have the necessary approvals in place to fluor idate the public water supply in accordance with 
New York State Public Health Law §1100-a. (Click on Laws at top bar; choose Laws of New 
York; scroll down to PHL – Public Health Law; enter 1100-a in search box and click “Search”.) 
 AND must  include Attachment 3  – Componenet B Technical S ubmittal for Propsals $50,000 or 
Less OR Attachment 4  – Component B Technical Submittal  for Projects $50,001 or More OR 
Projects Initiative Fluoridation. 
Please Note: Federal Government, Native American, private, and state-owned water systems are not 
eligible for this funding.  
Terms marked with *asterisk are further defined in Attachment 5  - Definitions Document . 
Eligible Municipalities w ill need to submit a separate applicatio n for each project and component.   

 
 
 
Drinking Water Fluoridation RFA – Rolling Submissions 
4 
 Eligible Municipalities can only submit an ap plication for one Component (either Component A 
or B) of this RFA at a time. If both Components are required for a municipality’s project, it is 
advised that the eligible municipality submit an application for Component A (Planning and 
Feasibility Projects) first. Once a successful eligible municipal ity has completed its Component A 
project (Engineering Repor t developed and final voucher and pr ogress report submitted to NYSDOH), 
an eligible municipality may then submit a separa te application for Component B (Implementation and 
Maintenance Projects). 
Submitted projects determined to not meet the requirements will be encouraged to resubmit again. 
 A. Available Funding 
 
The total funding available is $2.5 million annually. As stated in the Term of Contract (Section G), 24-
month term, with a start date approximately  six months from aw ard letter date.  
Component A applicants may request up to $50,000 for the full contract term. Total funding for 
Component A is projected to be  $500,000 annually for all awards.  
Component B applicants may requ est up to $1 million for the full contract term. Total funding for 
Component B is projected to be $2 million annually fo r all awards.  
Note:  If for any reason the applications  for either component do not full y utilize the allocated funding, 
the Department reserves the ri ght to reallocate sa vings from one component to another.  
Please Note: To ensure that projects will be  completed within the 24-month contract period, 
municipalities should consult with their local or NYSDOH  and initiate and/or obtain the necessary 
endorsements or approvals for their project sc ope/engineering report pr ior to submitting an 
application. 
This funding is for “new” projects  only, meaning any previously comp leted work, such as fluoridation 
system remodel in 2020, or work curr ently in progress, such as an E ngineering Report in development, 
is not eligible for reimbursemen t under this RFA. In addition, f unding may not be used to supplant 
funds for existing staff or ot her fluoridation activities. 
If funding becomes limited for any reason during the 6- year period of this RFA,  the project will be 
suspended with adequate notice in the NYS Contract Reporter. 
 
III. Project Narrative/Work Plan Outcomes 
 
Component A - Planning and Feasibility Projects support the development of an Engineering Report 
to: 
 Study the feasibility (technical and ec onomical) of starting fluoridation; OR, 
 Develop a technical plan fo r initiating fluoridation; OR, 
 Upgrade an existing fluoridation sy stem, including projects that have structural, chemical, or 
process modifications, that requires profes sional design services.

grants.title: Corrections Health Initiative: Navigation and Essential Support Services for Incarcerated Individuals and Reentrants
grants.summary: This grant funds navigation and support services for incarcerated individuals and reentrants, focusing on HIV and Hepatitis C care and reentry coordination.
grants.description: The Corrections Health Initiative provides funding for navigation and essential support services for incarcerated individuals and reentrants living with HIV and/or diagnosed with Hepatitis C. The program includes components for care in state correctional facilities, reentry coordination in the NYC area, and statewide networking, training, and resources. Applications must be submitted online via the NYS Grants Gateway. Not-for-profit applicants must maintain prequalification status to be eligible.
grants.eligibility_notes: Eligible applicants include not-for-profit organizations that are prequalified in the NYS Grants Gateway.
key_requirements: Applicants must be not-for-profit organizations.
Applicants must be prequalified in the NYS Grants Gateway.
Applications must be submitted online via the Grants Gateway.
Applicants must address the needs of individuals living with HIV and/or diagnosed with Hepatitis C.

2.0 OVERVIEW   
 
Through this Request for Proposals (RFP), the New York State Department of Health (the Department) is 
seeking competitive proposals from qualified bidders to support the work and activities of the Department’s 
New York State Perinatal Quality Collaborative (NYSPQC) with assistance in planning, developing, 
operationalizing, and evaluating the various projects of the NYSPQC as further detailed in Section 4.0 (Scope 
of Work) . It is the Department’s intent to award one (1) contract from this procurement. 
 2.1 Introductory Background 
 The Department,  as the lead State agency for maternal and child health programs, is issuing this RFP to 
identify a Contractor with the skills, abilities and resources to support the work and activities of the New York 
State Perinatal Quality Collaborative (NYSPQC).  
 The Contractor will provide the Department with:  
• Quality improvement (QI) expertise and guidance to assist with all aspects of the NYSPQC projects, based on the framework and recommendations of organizations such as the Institute for Healthcare 
Improvement (IHI) and Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ);  
• Ongoing, consistent faculty with clinical experience to serve as subject matter experts as well as guest 
speakers with lived experience, as needed to implement and sustain projects ;  
• Current research, evidence- based practice and standard of care, and information relevant to project 
focus areas to ensure project success;  
• Access to ad hoc guest speakers for NYSPQC educational events, such as speakers for Coaching Call webinars or educational webinars and in- person/virtual Learning Sessions; and  
• Access to parent/family partners as members of the NYSPQC team to implement and sustain projects . 
   

New York State Perinatal Quality Collaborative (NYSPQC)  
The NYSPQC  commenced in 2010 and is overseen by the Department’s Division of Family Health (DFH) . It is 
a nationally recognized initiative that engages a statewide network of birthing facilities that seek to provide the 
best, safest, and most equitable care for NYS’ birthing people and infants.  The NYSPQC aims to improve 
maternal and infant outcomes, reducing morbidity and mortality, by moving evidence- based guidelines to 
action through intervention- specific projects.  The NYSPQC works closely with state and national professional 
organizations and associations, community organizations, parent/family partners, and others.  The NYSPQC’s projects are offered at no cost to participating birthing facility teams.  
 The NYSPQC has adapted the Institute for Healthcare Improvements (IHI) model for Idealized Design of 
Perinatal Care and Breakthrough Series Methodology as a framework to guide improvement.
1, This model 
consists of the development of reliable clinical processes to manage perinatal care; uses principles that 
improve safety by preventing, detecting, and mitigating errors; and establishes prepared and activated care 
teams that communicate effecti vely with each other and with birthing people and families.  
 Specific priorities set by the Department are implemented by participating stakeholders, which include NYS 
birthing facilities, health care professionals, and community -based organizations.   Projects of the NYSPQC 
focus on improving outcomes for birthing people, families, and infants.  
 
Each project is conducted over a period of at least two years and continues until there is a consensus among 
project stakeholders to close the project, following the achievement of project deliverables.  The projects  are 
implemented using the Q uality Improvement (QI)  process . Each project includes at least two (2) virtual/in-
person Learning Sessions over the project timeline, with monthly technical assistance Coaching Call webinars . 
There is routine feedback of QI data submitted by project participants with discussions of successes and barriers and strategies for change. The feedback tim e frame is based on the focus of the specific project and 
frequency of health occurrence. There is also discussion of specific strategies to enable project participants to 
learn from each other’s experiences. A NYSPQC website has been established 
(health.ny.gov/community/pregnancy/nyspqc/ ) as well as project -specific Basecamps as a repository of project 
materials for participating birthing facility teams. Project -specific listservs have also been established for 
ongoing communication between NYSPQC staff and stakeholders, including birthing facility teams . 
 
The contractor will support current/ongoing NYSPQC projects , a maximum of four concurrent projects at any 
given time,  and their eventual closing, as well as the implementation and eventual closing of new projects.  
Current and potential areas of focus include but are not limited to:  
 
• Improving perinatal outcomes for Black birthing people as well as their experience of care during the 
birth hospitalization with a focus on reducing rates of Nulliparous, Term, Singleton, Vertex (NTSV) cesarean births to improve perinatal outcomes;  
• Improving outcomes for infants receiving care in NYS’ Neonatal Intensive Care Units (NICUs) as well 
as their parent’s/caregiver’s experience of care while their infant is being cared for in the NICU; and  
• Other perinatal priorities identified by the Department and NYSPQC to modify ongoing projects and/or develop new projects with a goal of improving birth and other maternal and child health outcomes.  
 
While the focus areas of the NYSPQC projects evolve, change and/or expand over time, and all must be approved by the Department, the general format and process of the learning collaborative for each intervention 
project  remains similar.  
  
 
1 Institute for Healthcare Improvement (IHI), Boston MA.

Any qualifications or exceptions proposed by a Bidder to this RFP  should be submitted in writing using the

2.3 Term of the Agreement  
 The term of the Contract that will be entered into pursuant to this RFP between the Department and the 
successful Bidder is expected to be for a period of five years co mmencing on the date shown on the Calendar 
of Events in 
Section 1, subject to the availability of sufficient funding, successful Contractor performance, and

The maximum allowable annual total bid price must not exceed $7 31,000 per contract year s 1 through 3, and
