3.0 BIDDERS’ QUALIFICATIONS TO PROPOSE  
 
3.1 Minimum Qualifications  
 The Department will accept proposals from bidders with the following types and levels of experience as a 
prime contractor:  
 
• Bidders must have a minimum of three (3) years of experience in healthcare- based QI /performance 
management;  
• Bidders must have a minimum of three (3) years of experience with the development of resources, 
services and evaluation related to healthcare- based QI/performance management;  and 
• Bidders must have three (3) years of experience with addressing health disparities in maternal and 
child health and working with culturally and ethnically diverse groups.  

 
Experience acquired concurrently is considered acceptable.  
 For the purposes of this RFP, a “prime contractor” is defined as one who has the contract with the owner of a 
project or job and has full responsibility for its completion. A prime contractor undertakes to perform a complete 
contract and may employ (and manage) one or more subcontractors to carry out specific parts of the contract.  
 
Failure to meet these Minimum Qualifications will result in a proposal being found non- responsive and 
eliminated from consideration.  
 
3.2 Preferred Qualifications  
 
The Department will provide additional points in scoring for proposals from bidders with the following types and 
levels of experience as a prime contractor:  
• A minimum of three (3) years of experience with involving individuals with lived experience and/or 
parent/family partners in development, administration and/or monitoring of learning collaboratives . 
 
4.0 SCOPE OF WORK  
 
This Section describes the NYSPQC consulting services  that are required to be provided by the selected 
bidder. The selected bidder must be able to provide all of these services throughout the contract term.  
 
PLEASE NOTE:  Bidders will be requested to provide responses that address all of the requirements of this 
RFP as part of its Technical Proposal.  
 The terms “bidders”, “vendors” and “proposers” are also used interchangeably. For purposes of this RFP, the 
use of the terms “shall”, “must” and “will” are used interchangeably when describing the Contractor’s/Bidder’s 
duties.  
 
4.1 Tasks/Deliverables  
 
4.1.1  Project Management  
 
The Contractor must  provide and coordinate a project management team which supports the planning, 
developing, implementing, operationalizing, summarizing, and evaluating of various  NYSPQC  projects.  
 
The Contractor’s project management team will provide targeted support to the Department as follows:  
• Provide assistance with the management of projects and administrative tasks related to the NYSPQC 
projects;  
• Provide technical assistance and support for meeting and webinar participants using the NYSPQC’s Zoom , Webex, or similar  platform for meetings and webinar events, including technical assistance in 
preparation for and during events, such as with creating links for pre- registration, troubleshooting 
connection issues for attendees, running in- webinar polls, answering questions  in chat, and generating 
attendance reports;  
• Coordinate activities of project management team members, as necessary, to ensure contract work is  
being completed;  
• Plan, create and distribute agendas and materials  (i.e., worksheets to facilitate team planning and 
implementation) , facilitate and attend meetings with stakeholders internal and external to Department, 
and provide written summaries of those meetings;  
• Organize project related materials, including forms and resources submitted by participating birthing facility teams, meeting agendas and summaries, project tools such as, but not limited to, Driver 
Diagrams and Change Packages, and Plan– Do-Study -Act (PDSA) Worksheets, a quality improvement 
tool used when running small tests of change ( https://www.ihi.org/resources/tools/plan- do-study -act-
pdsa- worksheet ); 
• Create and develop communication tools and resources (i.e., email updates, tables, and meeting 
summaries) for participating birthing facility teams and partners regarding project progress, and data, 

concerns , in consultation with Department;  
• Work with the Department to identify areas of concern or those requiring clarification from project 
participants;  
• Communicate progress and concerns related to data with Department as appropriate on a weekly or bi -
weekly basis;  
• Ensure communication with all project participants as identified by the Department, including drafting e-
mails related to project progress and updates, developing project summaries and presentations, and 
developing dissemination plans for these items;  
• Draft emails to be distributed by Department via project listservs to communicate with all project 
participants on all relevant updates, clarifications, upcoming meetings and events, and data reminders;  
• Create NYSPQC project summaries that consist of an analysis of the data collected as well as impact 
of strategies implemented through the course of the project to be shared with all project participants as 
requested by Department; and  
• Meet via phone and/or webinar with Department on a bi -weekly or as needed basis to ensure a mutual 
understanding of project progress, as well for in- person Learning Sessions.  
 
Project development activities include, but are not limited to:  
• Identifying emerging issues and best practices related to ongoing projects to ensure integration into 
project strategies;  
• Assist ing with the identification and selection of new project focus areas by researching clinical 
standards and emerging issues as requested by the Department;  
• Gathering literature as well as information from other state based PQCs on related topic areas;  
• Assist with the identification, engagement, and coordination of advisory work groups, including 
planning, hosting, facilitating, and evaluating meetings and events;  
• Develop up to  four (4) Recruitment Packages * for new projects over the five- year period, including 
developing other project materials  such as : project measures, Driver Diagram **, Change Packages ***, 
and other materials as appropriate; and  
• Develop materials for activities related to new and ongoing projects.  
 
*The Recruitment Package is a resource that defines the project in detail, outlines responsibilities, and 
describes the collaborative QI process. It contains the project schedule, the data to be collected in support of 
the project, the defined measures and the suggested compositi on of project teams. Once recruited, teams 
perform pre -work data collection for baseline measurement of the perinatal issue to be addressed during the 
project.  
 
**The Driver Diagram  is a visual display that depicts the relationship between the project aim, the primary 
drivers that contribute directly to achieving the aim, and the secondary drivers that are necessary to achieve 
the primary drivers. For more information about the Driver Diagram or other resources appropriate to this 
project, visit the Institute for Healthcare Improvement website at https://www.ihi.org/resources/tools/driver -
diagram . 
 
***The  Change Packag e includes a list of high leverage key change concepts or “ideas” for changes at the 
system level and specific strategies for those changes. These changes come from evidence provided by 
previous research. This “change package” is the basis for project parti cipants’ strategies that they will 
implement in their birthing facility to reach the project goal(s).  
 
  

 
4.1.2  Planning and Implementation of Learning Collaborative Project s 
 
The Contractor must  support ongoing projects and assist with the planning and implementation of the 
NYSPQC projects. This consists of planning for ongoing and new NYSPQC projects, preparing materials for 
Coaching Call webinars , educational webinars and Learning Sessions, and implementing IHI’s model for QI 
activities  related to each project . 
 
The Contractor must perform the following specific contract requirements to the satisfaction of the Department:  
• Support ongoing NYSPQC projects, and the development of new NYSPQC projects  to ensure 
objectives set by the Department are being met ; 
• Provide the Department with relevant information regarding maternal and child health and the 
outcomes the project is seeking to achieve (e.g. evidence behind the strategy to improve a maternal 
and child health outcome) to ensure continued project success;  
• Work with the Department to identify topic areas of concentration and guest speakers for Coaching Call 
webinars , educational webinars and Learning Sessions based on participant needs and progress;  
• Work with the Department to identify, engage, and coordinate advisory work group members, which will include the coordination of up to two in -person advisory work group meetings per year. Advisory work 
group members vary from project -to-project, and may include clinical providers, quality improvement 
experts, staff from professional and/or hospital associations, and parent family partners ;  
• Work with the Department to identify, engage, coordinate, and compensate local and national guest speakers for presentations during Coaching  Call webinar s, educational webinars and Learning 
Sessions ;   
• Work with the Department, clinical/content and QI guest speakers to ensure content of Coaching Call webinars , educational webinars and Learning Sessions are relevant , complete and provide information 
and guidance to assist project participants to improve their project strategies;  
• Assist in closing projects as appropriate, including writing project summaries that may include data 
analysis, summary of the evidence and strategies used by the project participants, successes and 
challenges as well as other components as requested by the Department to clearly depict the project as 
needed; and  
• Aid in disseminating the findings of NYSPQC projects as requested and approved by the Department such as, but not limited to, evaluation of quality improvement and project performance, implementation 
methods, assisting with design of project curriculum (i. e., Coaching Call webinars, educational 
webinars, Learning Sessions, etc.), and engaging and coordinating teams (i.e., high performers).  
 
4.1.3  Coaching Call Webinars and Educational Webinars  
 
Coaching Call webinars are generally one (1) hour webinars where Department, project participants, and 
contract staff meet to discuss project progress and strategies for improvement.   Typically, there is one 
Coaching Call webinar per month per NYSPQC project.  These webinars are opportunities for NYSPQC  project 
participants to connect with other participating birthing facility teams or stakeholders to share strategies, identify lessons learned, overcome barriers, recognize successes, and expedite the implementation of project 
goals.  
 Educational webinars are  one (1) hour webinars where Department and contract staff share content relative to 
NYSPQC projects  to educate participants, which include perinatal care providers and staff from NYS birthing 
facility teams.  Educational webinars are open to perinatal care providers and NYS birthing facility teams 
regardless of NYSPQC participation status.  
 The contractor must  support the Department with Coaching Call  webinars and educational webinar s on a 
focused maternal child health topic that are open to a broader audience which may include all NYS birthing facilities (regardless of project participation status and/or all NYS perinatal care providers).  
 
 
The Contractor must:  

• Collaborate with the Department to develop content for and participate in  Coaching Call webinars and 
Educational webinars;  
• Identify, engage, and coordinate guest speakers, such as national subject matter experts or 
participating birthing facility teams, for each webinar and in consultation with Department;  
• Assist with development of agendas, draft curriculum, and draft email notifications announcing the webinars as well as follow -up information;  and 
• Provide support for all NYSPQC project webinars, including, but not limited to, scheduling, loading 
slides, running webinar platform, troubleshooting issues with the webinar platform as technical 
difficulties arise, assisting project participants with technical issues preventing access or parti cipation, 
presenting, facilitating and/or moderating discussion, taking notes, providing summaries, and identifying 
next steps and action items . 
 
 
4.1.4  Learning Sessions  
 
In-person and/or virtual Learning Sessions occur approximately twice per year  per project  (in-person sessions 
are one -day meetings and virtual sessions are two days of two- hour webinars per day)  wherein  teams from all 
participating organizations and expert guest speakers convene to exchange ideas and learn from one another. 
Project participants may be provided with guidance and instruction by the QI Advisor s in using the Model for 
Improvement
2 to improve their performance in the project’s focus area. P roject participants have direct access 
to each other and to subject matter experts at these meetings to gain insight and new ideas. Hospital/health 
care project teams learn from each other as they report on their methods, successes, barriers, and lessons 
learned i n storyboard presentations and discussions. Depending on the number of facilities involved in a 
project, the number of Learning Session participants ranges from 30 to 200 attendees.  
 
The Contractor will:  
• Assist the D epartment with planning and conducting Learning Sessions;  
• Assist the Department with the development and coordination of agendas, materials and presentations;  
• Present and facilitate Learning Session discussions, as requested by Department;  
• Assist with the identification and engage ment  of guest speakers (who are not existing members of the 
project management team) to conduct presentations at virtual or in- person Learning Sessions ; and 
• Assist in conducting an analysis for the storyboard presentations at the close of each Learning Session.  
 
The Department will be responsible for arranging and providing the venue for the in- person Learning Sessions 
which will be held within NYS.  Other costs  associated with the Learning Sessions, including Contractor travel 
to/from and staffing at the event, guest speaker travel to/from the event and speaker fees are the responsibility 
of the Contractor , and must be included in the contractor’s bid pricing in Attachment B –  Cost Proposal.  
 
4.1.5  Clinical Quality Improvement  
 
The Contractor must  assist with developing and implementing interventions and materials related to the yearly 
projects of the NYSPQC, and work with the Department on those plans and materials. The Contractor must  
accomplish these specific tasks:  
 
• Provide QI Guidance  including : 
o Prepare annotated bibliographies of perinatal and infant health research pertinent to specified 
interventions;  
o Participate in the development and implementation of the NYSPQC work plans;  
o Provide advice regarding the learning process and its application to the NYSPQC; and  
o Prepare presentations and materials for workgroup meetings, Coaching Call and/or  educational 
webinars, and Learning Sessions . 
 
 
2 The Model for Improvement was developed by Associates in Process Improvement. 
www.apiweb.org/API_home_page.htm.  

• Develop Performance Improvement Interventions and Change Packages including : 
o Provide up- to-date project -related information to the Department and NYSPQC project 
participants as requested by Department;  
o Assist with the identification and selection of performance improvement interventions;  
o Develop change packages to support the clinical performance improvement interventions;   
• Utilize the Institute  for Healthcare Improvement’s Breakthrough Series improvement methodology 
(https://www.ihi.org/resources/white -papers/breakthrough -series -ihis-collaborative- model -achieving-
breakthrough)  to guide projects and assist both the NYSPQC and participating NYS birthing facilities in 
achieving objectives ; and  
o Provide expertise and practical guidance in quality improvement methodology implementation to 
the NYSPQC team at the Department, as well as to participating birthing facility teams . 
 
• Advise on Data Collection and Measurement Strategies including:  
o Assist with data collection strategies for the NYSPQC workgroups and teams;  
o Provide clinical and evaluation expertise to support data collection and measurement strategies 
needed to assess the effectiveness of the interventions; and  
o Review Department analysis of project data to help identify areas for data collection and 
measurement improvement . 
 
Quality improvement data are collected by the Department through the Health Commerce System 
(HCS).  The contractor will serve in an advisory capacity concerning project subject matter, 
measurement definition, and interpretation, but will not be involved in directly collecting and/or 
analyzing the data.  
 
• Provide Communication and Learning Strategies:  
o Facilitate communication among the NYSPQC advisory work group and participating birthing 
facility teams during the project meetings, Coaching Calls and/or educational webinars, and 
Learning Sessions;  
o Prepare project summaries, as requested by Department, to disseminate findings and lessons 
learned; and  
o Communicate via telephone, email, and/or webinar on a weekly basis as needed with the Department NYSPQC program team regarding progress, to discuss any questions or concerns, 
and to plan for next steps. In addition, the Clinical Leaders will communicate wi th the NYSPQC 
Project Director on an as needed basis to ensure appropriate progress and clear lines of 
communication.  
 4.1.6  Quality Improvement  Advisement  
 
The Contractor must  provide QI advisement for the development and implementation of all interventions and 
materials related to the project, and work with the Department on those plans and materials. The Contractor will be responsible for these specific tasks:  
 
• QI Guidance:  
o Arrange, host and facilitate virtual meetings and bi -weekly conference calls with the 
Department;  
o Prepare annotated bibliographies of perinatal and children’s research pertinent to specified 
interventions;  
o Participate in the development and implementation of the NYSPQC project work plans;  
o Provide guidance regarding the learning process and its application to the NYSPQC project 
participants;  
o Prepare presentations and materials for workgroup meetings and Learning Sessions;  
o Assist the Department with identifying, planning, and executing improvement projects;  
o Interact with project participants, which may include hospital/health care teams, community -
based organizations, etc., as needed, to support and facilitate QI projects; and 
o Provide technical assistance to project participants to  prepare project participants to share their 
progress on Coaching Call webinars . 

 
• Interventions and Change Packages:  
o Provide up- to-date clinical information to the Department and NYSPQC project participants;  
o Assist with the identification and selection of clinical interventions;  
o Develop change packages and other relevant materials to support the clinical interventions; and  
o Provide QI guidance for data collection and measurement strategies needed to assess the 
effectiveness of the interventions . 
 
• Data Strategies:  
o Assist with the development and implementation of data collection strategies for NYSPQC 
workgroups and teams;  
o Provide clinical expertise to support data collection and measurement strategies needed to 
assess the effectiveness of the interventions;  
o Review DOH analysis of project data and help identify areas for improvement; and  
o Provide suggestions for data analysis and evaluation regarding QI methods (i.e., funnel charts, etc.). 
 
• Communication and Learning Strategies:  
o Attend and facilitate communication among the NYSPQC workgroups and teams during the 
project meetings, Coaching Call and educational webinars, and Learning Sessions;  
o Assist in the preparation of project summaries, to  disseminate findings and lessons learned; and  
o The QI Advisor s will participate in conference calls on a bi -weekly basis with the Department to 
share progress and contribution to the NYSPQC projects.  
 4.1.7  Administration of Learning Collaborative  
 The Contractor must  perform the following specific contract requirements:  
• Provide the Department with access to expert QI guest speakers with perinatal and children’s health 
clinical and/or lived expertise, as well as content experts, as needed to implement additional QI 
projects , during in- person and virtual meetings, webinars,  and conference calls ; 
• Work with NYSPQC project participants to ensure an understanding of QI;  
• Provide QI coaching via phone or webinar , including one- on-one with participating birthing facility teams 
as necessary (approximately four per month), small groups of participating facilities (estimated two per 
month), and hosting at least two hours per month of open office hours via webinar;  and 
 
The Contractor must deliver, address, and collaborate with the Department regarding the deliverables and 
project components listed above in Section 4.1 These deliverables are to be completed at the request of the 
Department , and the Department reserves the right to alter any of these deliverables, as needed, to fit the 
current Scope of Work (SOW).  Changes to the SOW will need to be made as amendments to the contract as 
indicated in item I.D. of the Standard Contract (Attachm ent 8) , and subject to review and approval by the AG 
and OSC.  
 
Note:  The contractor is responsible for effectuating contractual agreements with guest speakers  and 
parent/family partners,  and paying all travel costs and attendance/presentation fees  directly to the guest 
speaker. For each guest speaker utilized, the C ontract or will bill the Department the fixed hourly price in the 
Cost Proposal, and this will be the only means of contractor reimbursement for the utilization of guest 
speakers.  
  
 
  
 
 
 
 

 
4.2 Staffing  
 The Contractor must provide the Department with a project management team that has the capacity to fulfill all 
the required tasks and deliverables. Key staff that comprise the project management team provided by the 
Contractor will include:  
 
• One (1) Project Director;  
• One (1) Project Assistant/Coordinator;  
• Clinical Leaders including at least  one (1) specializing in obstetrics and at least  one (1) specializing in 
neonatology;  
• One (1) Equity Leader; and 
• At least one (1) QI Advisor.  
 
The minimum qualifications for key staff are defined below. The Department reserves the right to approve 
candidates for project management team positions upon contract award.  
 
Required experience of key staff can be obtained concurrently. Key staff are also required to attend conference 
calls/webinars with Department staff bi -weekly or as needed and participate in the various NYSPQC 
workgroups as advised. The project management team, which includes the QI Advisor s, will be expected to 
attend relevant virtual/in- person meetings, conference calls and webinars as requested by the Department.  
 
Note:  Reimbursement for staff time and all related travel costs for positions identified within this RFP Section 
4.2 shall be paid to the contractor at the hourly rate bid in the Cost Proposal. This is the only means of 
reimbursement the contractor will receive.  
 
4.2.1  Project Director  
 The Contractor must designate a Project Director who will work closely with the Department and its designees 
to oversee and direct the contractor team, oversee and coordinate all aspects of the consultant team’s work , 
and facilitate the exchange of necessary information with the Department . The Project Director will be 
responsible for managing and coordinating the project management team, ensuring all RFP requirements  are 
met in a timely fashion, communicating with designated Department staff as appropriate, and all other specified 
tasks specified in Section 4.1. The Project Director must  have experience in the management of a large multi -
stakeholder project or initiative (i.e., within an organization, hospital system, or state) , preferably related to 
maternal and child health.  Additionally, the Project Director must  be experienced in the practice of QI.  The 
Project Director must have at least five (5) years of experience in program or project management and can anticipate devoting a total of 20  hours per week, or 1,040 hours per year, to this project.  
 
The Project Director will:  
• Attend NYSPQC project team meetings and actively participate in project planning, implementation, 
and evaluation activities during these meetings;  
• Attend and participate in meetings with the Department and NYSPQC stakeholders, such as birthing 
facility teams and professional organizations, in support of project planning, implementation and evaluation activities ; 
• Collaborate with the Department to develop content for and participate  in Coaching Call webinars , 
educational webinars , and Learning Sessions, including presenting  and facilitating discussions ; 
• Identify, engage, and coordinate guest speakers  for webinar s as appropriate and in consultation with 
Department;  
• Assist in identification,  and recruitment of, establish contracts with, obtain receipts and other 
documentation, and provide payment to guest speakers , for their presentation during Coaching Calls 
and Learning Sessions, and arrange for and provide payment to clinical lead s, parent/family partners,  
and QI Advisor s, and all subcontracted members of the contractor team  (as defined in § 4.2.5 of this 
RFP) ;  
• Oversee and manage all travel expenses incurred by attending project management team members (all 
members do not attend all meetings as the Clinical leaders and QI Advisor s only attend when 

participation is relevant to the topic), including collection and review of supporting travel documentation, 
and authorizing payment for travel expenses including round- trip transportation, hotel accommodations, 
meals, and other incidentals for each in- person Learning Session. R eimbursement for all travel costs 
must be included in the hourly bid rates for staffing. There will be no other means of reimbursing for 
travel expenses. ; and  
• Ensure bi -weekly meetings are scheduled and held with designated staff at the Department to discuss 
project status, updates and next steps.  
 
4.2.2  Project Coordinator  
 The Contractor must assign a Project Coordinator who will work closely with the Project Director, the 
Department and its designees to assist with coordination of all aspects of this project and to facilitate the 
exchange of necessary information. The Proje ct Coordinator will be responsible for supporting the Project 
Director with managing and coordinating the project management team, ensuring all RFP deliverables are met 
in required timeframes , communicating with designated Department staff as appropriate, and all other tasks 
specified in Section 4.1. The Project Coordinator must have relevant experience in project coordination and 
strong communication skills .  The Project Coordinator must  have at least three (3) years of experience in 
program or project management and can  anticipate devoting a total of 20 hours per week, or 1,040  hours per 
year, to this project.  
 
The Project Coordinator will: 
• Provide coordination of NYSPQC planning meetings which may include staff from the Department, clinical advisors, parent/family partners , guest speakers , the contractor team, and other stakeholders.  
This will include: development of agendas; drafting educational curriculum planning documents; drafting 
e-mail notifications  and follow -ups to stakeholders; coordination and updates of project work plans and 
timelines ; and ongoing communication with the Department related to these items ; 
• Collaborate with the Department to develop content for and participate in Coaching Call webinars, educational webinars, and Learning Sessions .  Prior to such events, this will include: scheduling 
webinars and events ; coordination of agenda development, coordination of slide decks  and resources ; 
coordination of participating clinical leaders, parent/family partners, and guest speakers ; and 
communication with Department staff related to outstanding issues and finalized event documents .  
During and following events this will include : loading slides ; running webinar platform ; troubleshooting 
issues with the webinar platform as technical difficulties arise ; assisting project participants with 
technical issues prevent ing access or participation;  presenting;  facilitating and/or moderating 
discussion ; taking notes ; providing summaries ; tracking participation and attendance ; and identifying 
next steps and action items.  
 
4.2.3  Clinical Leaders  
 
The Contractor must  assist in identifying and contract ing with a minimum of two (2) clinical leaders for specific 
projects who will oversee the tasks outlined in Section 4.1. 4.  The Clinical Leaders must be board 
certified/board eligible physicians with at least five (5) years of experience in QI related to perinatal health care. 
Clinical leaders may have specialties in maternal -fetal medicine, obstetrics and/or gynecology, pediatrics , 
neonatology , or addiction medicine. The Clinical Leaders ’ activities will be specified per p roject. Clinical 
Leaders will be subject to Department approval. The anticipated time for Clinical Leaders to devote on projects 
are expected to be 120 hours per year.  The costs for all Clinical Leaders will be paid by the contractor to the 
contracted individuals , and these costs must be included in the contractor’s pricing submitted in Attachment B 
– Cost Proposal. There will be no other means of payment to the contractor for Clinical Leaders other than the 
rates identified in the Cost Proposal.  
 
Additional clinical leadership may be required on an ad hoc basis in other areas  such as on Coaching Call 
webinars, educational webinars, at Learning Sessions, or with resource review . Other Clinical Leaders, such 
as physicians, nurses, midwives, PAs, psychologists, etc., may provide additional clinical leadership in specific 
areas.  
 
4.2.4  Equity Leader  

 
The Contractor must  provide an Equity Leader to participate in all projects of the NYSPQC.  The Equity Leader 
will assist with all tasks outlined in Section 4.1 and be responsible for providing leadership and technical expertise related to equity in the development and implementation of all NYSPQC projects. Key responsibilities 
for this role include, but are not limited to, ensuring equity remains at the forefront of all new and ongoing 
NYSPQC projects including in each project’s goals and objectives, data collection and meas urement 
strategies, Driver Diagrams as well as curriculum design and development, and providing ongoing training, 
consultation and monitoring of participating project teams in all NYSPQC projects. The Equity Leader must 
have at least five (5) years of expe rience in the focused area of maternal and infant/child health equity and/or 
perinatal equity. It is preferred that the Equity Leader also have at least five (5) years of experience serving as the Equity Leader for a large- scale QI initiative within an organization, hospital system, or state,  that provided 
coaching and technical assistance activities. The Equity Leader will work an average of 65 hours  per month, 
depending on the activities to be completed each month.  
 
4.2.5  QI Advisor s 
 
The Contractor must  assign at least one, maybe  up to two  QI Advisor s, who will be selected in collaboration 
with the Department,  to perform and oversee the tasks outlined in Section 4.1.6.  The QI Advisor s will be 
responsible for providing leadership and technical expertise in the implementation of all relative NYSPQC 
projects. Key responsibilities for this role include but are not limited to conducting data -driven QI coaching, 
ongoing training, consultation and monitoring of project participants , and a ssist in conducting an analysis for 
the storyboard presentations at the close of each Learning Session for relative NYSPQC projects. The QI 
Advisor s must  have at least five (5) years of experience in perinatal  QI. It is preferred that the QI Advisor s also 
have at least five (5) years of perinatal clinical experience and experience serving as the advisor for a large-scale QI initiative within an organization, hospital system, or state,  that provided coaching and technical 
assistance activities. In total, the QI Advisor s will work an average of 30 hours  per month  per QI advisor , 
depending on the activities to be completed each month.  
 
4.3 Reporting  
 
The Contractor must  submit quarterly progress reports. The progress report s need to detail the Contractor’s 
progress with the contract deliverables detailed in Section 4.1.  Quarterly progress reports must be submitted 
within  30 days after the end of the contract  quarter or payment of subsequent voucher s will not be made until 
the progress report and all other supporting documentation required is submitted.   
 4.4 Information Technology 
 
The application and all systems and components supporting it, including, but not limited to , any forms and 
databases that include Personal Health, Personal Identification or other New York State information, must comply with all NYS security policies and standards listed at http://its.ny.gov/tables/technologypolicyindex.htm . 
 
4.5 Security  
 The selected Contractor shall comply with all privacy and security policies and procedures of the Department 
(https://its.ny.gov/policies ) and applicable State and Federal law and administrative guidance with respect to 
the performance of the Contract. The Contractor is required, if applicable, to execute a number of security and 
privacy agreements with the Department including a Business A ssociate Agreement (Appendix H) and a Data 
Use Agreement (DUA) at contract signing.  
 
The Contractor is expected to provide secure and confidential backup, storage and transmission for hard copy 
and electronically stored information. Under no circumstances will any records be released to any person, 
agency, or organization without specific written permission of the Department . The Contractor is obligated to 
ensure any Subcontractor hired by Contractor who stores, processes, analyzes or transmits MCD on behalf of 
Contractor has the appropriate security requirements in place. Contractor is required to include in all

grants.title: Helen Hayes Hospital Security Director
grants.summary: This grant funds the procurement of a security director for Helen Hayes Hospital to oversee safety and security operations.
grants.description: The purpose of this grant is to secure a qualified security director for Helen Hayes Hospital in West Haverstraw, New York. The selected individual or organization will be responsible for managing safety, security equipment, emergency management services, and life safety protocols. 2.0 OVERVIEW   
 Through this Request for Proposals ( RFP), the New York State Department of Health (the Department ) is 
seeking competitive proposals from qualified bidders to provide one (1) full time Security Director  at Helen 
Hayes Hospital as further detailed in Section 4.0 (Scope of Work).  It is the Department’s intent to award one 
(1) contract from this procurement.  
 2.1 Introductory Background 
  Helen Hayes Hospital is a 155-bed rehabilitation Hospital, consisting of 106 inpatient rehabilitation facility beds, 
25 Skilled Nursing Facility beds and 24 Transitional Care beds, located in Rockland County, Rt. 9W, West 
Haverstraw,  New York 10993.  It is part of the New York State Department of Health.  The Hospital offers ca re 
and treatment to people of all ages with physical disabilities and chronic disabling diseases.  
 The Security Director provides oversight of all security operations and Security personnel at Helen Hayes 
Hospital.  Helen Hayes Hospital has built a reputation of being one of the national leaders in physical 
rehabilitation and has maintained that reputation and standard of care with our Environment of Care and Life Safety programs run by our Security  Director. The Security Director is critical in ensuring the Hospital maintains 
a safe and secure environment for all who enter its premises. The Security Director is tasked with the 
development, implementation and adherence to security policies, procedures, protocols and the Hospitals’ 
Emergency Management program. The Security Director provides direction and guidance in disaster mitigation, 
preparation, response and recovery and conducts disaster drills to ensure Hospital staff are properly prepa red 
to handle internal and external disaster events, and works closely with state and local emergency management offices and state and local law enforcement, fire, and EMS. Functions under this important role include, but a re not limited to, conducting mandatory security and fire safety drills, assessment of response and deficiencies, implementing performance improvement, identifying areas of improvement, liaison with law enforcement and 
emergency services, risk assessment and security audits, security reports, logs and mandatory documenta tion 
as required by the New York State Department of Health, The Joint Commission, and federal statutes. This 
position fosters a patient care and work environment built on safe work practices and a work environment free from workplace violence and workplace hazards.

 The Bidder must  review, and is requested to have its legal counsel review, Attachment 8 , the DOH Agreement 
(Standard Contract), as the successful Bidder must be willing to enter into the Contract awarded pursuant to this RFP  in the terms of Attachment 8 , subject only to any amendments to the Standard Contract agreed 
by the Department during the Question and Answer Phase of this RFP  (see ,  Section 5.2) . Please note 
that this RFP  and the awarded Bidder’s Bid will become part of the Contract as Appendix B and C, 
respectively.  It should be noted that  Appendix A of Attachment 8 , “Standard Clauses for New York State Contracts”, 
contains important information, terms and conditions related to the Contract to be entered into as a result of this RFP  and will be incorporated, without change or amendment , into the Contract entered into between 
the Department and the successful Bidder. By submitting a response to this RFP , the Bidder agrees to comply 
with all the provisions of the Contract, including all of the provisions of Appendix A.  
 Note,  Attachment 7 , the Bidder’s Certified Statements, must  be submitted by each Bidder and includes a 
statement that the Bidder accepts, without any added conditions, qualifications or exceptions,  the 
contract terms and conditions contained in this RFP  including any exhibits and attachments, including, without 
limitation,  Attachment 8 . It also includes a statement that the Bidder acknowledges that, should any alternative 
proposals or extraneous terms be submitted with its Bid, such alternate proposals or extraneous terms will not be evaluated by the Department .  
 
Any qualifications or exceptions proposed by a Bidder to this RFP  should be submitted in writing using the 
process set forth in Section 5.2 (Questions) prior to the deadline for submission of written questions indicated 
in Section 1.  (Calendar of Events). Any such qualifications or exceptions that are not proposed prior to the 
deadline for the submission of written questions will not be considered by the Department  after contract award. 
Any amendments the Department  makes to the RFP  as a result of questions and answers will be publicized on 
the Department’s  web site and will be available and applicable to all Bidders equally.  
 
2.3 Term of the Agreement  
 The term of the Contract that will be entered into pursuant to this RFP between the Department and the successful Bidder is expected to be for a period of five (5) years  commencing on the date shown on the 
Calendar of Events in 
Section 1 , subject to the availability of sufficient funding, successful Contractor 
performance, and approvals from the New York State Attorney General (AG) and the Office of the State 
Comptroller (OSC).  
 
3.0 BIDDERS’ MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS TO PROPOSE  
 
The Department  will only accept bid proposals from bidders who meet all minimum requirements.   
 
• Bidder must be a company or a n agency having three (3)  years’ experience with placement of  Security 
Directors  with at least two (2) years of post -degree experience in the area of  safety and security  in a 
Hospital or healthcare setting.    
• Bidder must have three (3) years’ experience with placement of Sec urity Directors  with at least two (2) 
years’ experience overseeing an Emergency Management program, one (1) year of which must have 
been in a H ospital setting. 
• Bidder must have three (3) years’ experience with placement of Security Directors  with at least two (2) 
years’ experience in Environment of Care and Life Safety programs. 
 
Failure to meet these Minimum Qualifications will result in a proposal being found non- responsive and 
eliminated from consideration.  
 
Experience acquired concurrently is considered acceptable.  

6  
3.1 Definitions  
 
For the purposes of this RFP, the following terms shall have the following definitions: 
  
“Emergency Management program ” shall mean  the direction and guidance in disaster mitigation, preparation, 
response and recovery and conducts disaster drills to ensure Hospital staff are properly prepared to handle 
internal and external disaster events, and works closely with state and local emergency management offices a nd state and local law enforcement, fire, and EMS.  
 “Environment of Care and Life Safety Program ” shall mean  programs that are essential components  of 
healthcare facilities to ensure a safe and effective environment for patients, staff, and visitors.  These progra ms 
focus on managing the physical setting where patient treatment occ urs. 
 “Hospital Safety Program ” shall mean  a structured framework designed to prevent, mitigate, and report harmful 
incidents to patients, staff, and visitors during healthcare delivery.  “Hospital Setting ” shall mean  a structured e nvironment where medical care is provided to patients, 
encompassing various services, departments, and healthcare professionals dedicated for the care and  
treatment    of people with disabilities and chronic disabling diseases.  
 
For the purposes of this RFP, a “prime contractor” is defined as one who has the contract with the owner of a project or job and has full responsibility for its completion. A prime contractor undertakes to perform a complete contract and may employ (and manage) one or more subcontractors to carry out specific parts of the contract.  
 
 
4.0 SCOPE OF WORK  
 
This Section describes the services that are required to be provided by the candidate from the selected Bidder. 
The selected B idder must be able to provide a candidate of whom is qualified to perform  all of these services 
throughout the contract term.   PLEASE NOTE:  Bidders will be requested to provide responses that address all of  the requirements of this 
RFP as part of its Technical Proposal.   The terms “ Bidders”, “ Vendors” , “Contractors ” and “ Proposers” are also used interchangeably. For purposes of 
this RFP, the use of the terms “shall”, “must” and “will” are used interchangeably when describing the Contractor’s/Bidder’s duties.   4.1 Tasks/Deliverables 
  
4.1.1 Location and Scope of Work:  
 
The Contractor must  provide one full -time Security Director who will report to the Helen Hayes Hospital, 
located at 51- 55 N Route 9W, West Haverstraw, New York 10993.  
 
The Security Director must report five (5) days a week, Mondays through Fridays, eight (8) hours a day from 
8:00am to 5:00pm with a one- hour unpaid lunch period. In addition, the Contractor must ensure availability of 
the Security Director to be responsive to emergencies as needed on nights, weekends and holidays. Currently 
the Hospital permits the Security Director to request an alternate schedule in the event of an emergency need. 
The position would follow the same New York State holidays which in general  are New Year’s Day, Dr. Martin 
Luther King, Jr. Day, Washington’s Birthday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, 
Columbus Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day.  
 

7 The full-time Security Director will be responsible for managing, providing required reporting as listed in 
Section 4.3, overseeing and operationalizing the Hospital’s overall safety program, including management of  
approximately  15 Hospital Safety Officers. Specific duties are as follows:  
 
4.1.1.1  Safety Department  
 Performs supervisory and managerial functions of the Safety Department  and its safety officers . Train s all new 
safety and security employees  utilizing t raining materials already established by the Hospital.  Coordinates 
various safety and security trainings for the Safety Department.  Monitors and inspects safety and security 
employee work performance to assure performance standards are maintained through use of computer records. Schedules Safety staff and review s time and attendance, overtime usage and billable hours of safety 
subcontractors.  Assigns and distributes  work to safety and security staff. Establishes and coordinates weekly 
safety and security employee work schedule to assure necessary staff coverage.  Approves and verifies 
coordinated scheduled vacations and holidays and time off requests of safety and security personnel.  Evaluates, 
assesses and analyzes performance of safety and security personnel and reports results to the Director of 
Facilities Management and senior management. Oversees safety and security staff who screen visitors before 
allowing them to enter the premises.  Handles Human Resources matters, in conjunction with Director of Huma n Resources, in relation to employee performance, disciplinary action, recruitment and retention. Ensures 
compliance of applicable policies and regulations while implementing safety and security measures.  Communicates with patients, residents, families, visitors and staff in a professional manner.   4.1.1. 2
   Security Equipment  
 Ensures all security equipment, such as two- way radios and the H ospital security camera system, and any other 
security equipment  assigned to the Safety Department are in good working condition. The Hospital’s  Saf ety 
Officers do not carry or possess a weapon as part of their responsibilities . Maintains and monitors the Safety 
Department work order system.   Maintains flow and quality of work to assure timely completion of assigned 
workload and adherence to standards of quality control.   
 
4.1.1. 3
 Emergency Management Services 
 Directs the Hospital’s Emergency Management Program.  Provides guidance in disaster mitigation, preparation, response and recovery; works closely with state and local Office of Emergency Management (OEM) managers; 
prepares and conducts disaster drills and recommends improvement to committees, the Administrator and 
Director of Facilities Management. Serves as liaison between State & local Law Enforcement, Fire, EMS and Rockland County office of Emergency Management.  
 
4.1.1. 4 Life Safety  and Physical Environment  
 
Works with the Director of Facilities Management in meeting all Hospital Life Safety requirements and goals.  
Attends Environment of Care Committee  meetings , reports o n compliance with T JC and Department  standards 
and local authorities.  Oversees life safety inspections and other applicable areas to ensure compliance with TJC 
standards.  Plans, organizes, and controls the safety protocol of the H ospital under the guidelines of the Director 
of Facilities Management to keep staff engaged in operating, maintaining, repairing and renovating Hospital’s 
plant and facilities. Reviews and evaluates existing methods, systems, programs, practices, and procedures. 
Develops a plan of action that addresses any deficient  controls and submits recommendations including target 
start dates of new procedures to the Director of Facilities Management. Guides start -up of new and/or modifies 
methods, systems, programs, and practices within target timeframe. All controls will be consistent with federa l and state policies and standards.   Evaluates  and updates , at least annually,  the Hospital’s existing safety 
procedure plan and programs and recommends modifications and new program guidelines to comply with TJC 
standards and State and Federal Regulations.   
 4.1.1. 5
 Employee Orientation and Education 
 

8 Instructs new H ospital employees as part of the Hospital’s New Employee Orientation. Meets with Department 
Heads and Administrative staff to evaluate and explain current safety issues and the goals and objectives of the 
facility. Assists Department Heads and subcommittees in the development and implementation of preventative 
measures to reduce accidents and injuries.   Educates Hospital  staff, as needed, throughout the year on safety 
and security matters.    4.2 S taffing  
 
The Contractor is required to provide one (1) full time Security Director.  The Security Director will serve as the 
primary contact person for the Department.   
 
Within 30 days of the contract award, or not later than sixty (60)  days before the commencement date of the 
Contract Term, whichever is later, the Contractor will submit to the Department for review and approval not 
fewer than three (3) resumes of candidates for the position of the Director of Security, with references and 
other supporting documentation confirming that each proposed candidate satisfies the qualifications referred to 
in Section 4.2.1  and is otherwise an appropriate candidate to perform the tasks/deliverables enumerated in 
Subsection 4.1, sub- subsections 4.1.1.1  through 4.1. 1.5. The Department shall have the discretion to permit 
the Contractor to supply less than three (3) candidates.  
 
In the event an employee is found by the Contractor to not be performing at a level consistent with expected 
standards, the Contractor will provide such employee with warnings and/or termination notice.  
 
The Contractor will be responsible for approving or denying time off requests presented by the Contractor’s 
employees. The Contractor shall notify the DOH designee of the time off request and confirm with DOH prior to 
approving such time off requests. It s hall be the Contractor’s responsibility to ensure that DOH staffing needs 
are fully and competently covered at all times, regardless of the Contractor’s employees’ vacation, leave 
requests and/or other scheduled or unscheduled absences. The Contractor will  consult with the DOH designee 
before approving leave requests. Any unplanned absences by the Contractor’s staff must be reported by the 
contracted staff to both the Contractor and the DOH designee within in 1 hour of designated start time.  
 
The Contractor will provide all of the benefits required by State and Federal Labor laws, including:  
 
• Leave as required by law, including but not limited to the New York State Paid Family Leave Act, New 
York Mandatory Sick Leave Law, New York City's Paid Safe and Sick Leave Law, the Westchester 
County Earned Sick Leave Law, and any other applicable federal, State and local laws that mandates 
employers provide paid time off;  
• Emergency paid sick leave; 
• Medical insurance as required by law; and 
• Any optional employee- paid benefits offered by vendor at no additional cost to the state.  
 
It is understood and agreed that the contractor and its employees are independently employed, and in no 
manner, shall they be deemed employees of the New York State Department of Health, and therefore are not 
entitled to any of the benefits associated with such employment.  
 4.2.
1 Contracted Staff Qualifications 
 
The Security Director provided must meet the following experience and educational requirements:  
 
• An associate’s degree in criminal justice OR four (4) years of experience in police work or public safety  
• A minimum of two (2) years of experience working in a H ospital  or healthcare setting 
• A minimum of two (2) years of experience overseeing an Emergency Management program, one (1) 
year of which must have been in a Hospital setting 
• A minimum of two (2) years of experience in Environment of Care and Life Safety Programs  

9  
4.2.2 Changes in Staffing  
 
It
 is anticipated that all staff hired for this contract will be employed for the entire duration of the assignment per 
the contract. However, if staff voluntarily or involuntarily leave their assignment, the Contractor must replace staff 
as described in Section 4.2. If either the Contractor, or the Department, for any reason, deems that a contracted staff member must be removed from their assignment prior to the completion of this contract, each party shall 
mutually agree that remov al shall take place.  
 
4.3 Reporting  
 
The Contractor  is responsible for establishing and maintaining a system to produce monthly, quarterly, annual 
and/or other reports as may be required by the Department.  Monthly data reports are due fifteen (15) calenda r 
days following the end of each calendar month. Quarterly data reports are due fifteen (15) calendar days following the end of each state Fiscal Quarter. Bi -annual data reports are due fifteen (15) calendar  days following 
the end of each six -month period.  Yearly data reports are due fifteen (15) calendar  days following the end of 
each calendar or fiscal state year.  
 The comprehensive safety and security reports to be compiled for  the Director of Facilities Management include, 
but are not limited to:  
 
Immediately  
• Emergency Management Event After -Action Reports  
 
Daily  
• Security Reports for Rapid Response Team (RRT), Code Grey, H ospital  incidents requiring written 
reports  
• Streetlights and Campus Lighting Status

• Vehicle Logs Evaluations  
 Quarterly

• Parking Permit Reviews  
• Emergency Management Planned Drill After -Action Reports  
• Emergency Management Environment of Care Committee Update 
 Bi-Annually  
• DOH Review Results  
 Annual ly
 
• The New York State Evacuation of Facilities in Disasters System (NYS e- FINDS) Reporters Review , an 
emergency location tracking system for H ospital patients and nursing home and adult care facility 
residents that is utilized during facility evacuations  

10 • Safety Inventory Control  
• Safety Statistics  
 
4.4 Information Technology  
 
The Contractor shall ensure that any software or digital application utilized in the performance of duties under this contract is properly licensed, authorized, and fully compliant with all applicable federal and state regulations, including, but not limited to, the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health (HITECH) Act, and any corresponding New York State data privacy and security requirements.  
 All software and related systems must conform to recognized industry standards for cybersecurity, data integrity, and access control. This requirement applies to all systems, forms, databases and or applications that collect, store, transmit, or otherwise process data related to the H ospital’s operations, including any information 
containing or derived from Protected Health Information (PHI) , Personal Identification or other New York State 
information, and must comply with all NYS security policies and standards listed at http://its.ny.gov/tables/technologypolicyindex.htm .  The Contractor shall ensure that appropriate administrative, 
technical, and physical safeguards are in place to prevent unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, PHI or other confidential information.  
 
Upon request, the Contractor shall provide documentation verifying software licensing, compliance 
certifications, and the implementation of safeguards consistent with federal information security policies and compliance  with all NYS security policies and standards listed at 
http://its.ny.gov/tables/technologypolicyindex.htm  
 4.5 Security  
 The selected Contractor shall comply with all privacy and security policies and procedures of the Department (https://its.ny.gov/policies ) and applicable State and Federal law and administrative guidance with respect to 
the performance of the Contract. The Contractor is required, if applicable, to execute a number of security and privacy agreements with the Department including a Business Associate Agreement (Appendix H) and a Data 
Use Agreement (DUA) at contract signing.  
 
The Contractor is expected to provide secure and confidential backup, storage and transmission for hard copy and electronically stored information. Under no circumstances will any records be released to any person, agency, or organization without specific written permission of the Department . If any breach or suspected 
breach of the data or confidentiality occurs  the Department  must be notified immediately.  
 The Contractor is required to maintain and provide to the Department upon request their data confidentiality plans and procedures for meeting security requirements as they relate to the deliverables and services within this RFP .  
 Contractor  will develop and maintain adequate fully trained staff to respond to all stakeholder inquiries while 
protecting confidentiality and maintaining the security and integrity of all systems. Staff must be trained to 
understand and observe requirements related to confidentiality and operating guidelines for functions included in this RFP.  
 
The Contractor will comply fully with all current and future updates of the security procedures of the 
Department  as well as with all applicable State and Federal requirements, in performance of the Contract.  
   4.6 Transition   
 
The transition represents a period when the current contract activities performed by the Contractor must be 
turned over to the Department, another Department agent, or successor Contractor during or at the end of the contract term.  

11  
The Contractor shall ensure that any transition to the Department, Departmental agency or successor 
Contractor be done in a way that provides the Department with uninterrupted Se curity Director services. This 
includes a complete and total transfer of all data, files, reports, and records generated from the inception of the 
Contract through the end of the Contract to the Department or another Department agent should that be required during or upon expiration of its contract.  
 
The Contractor shall provide technical and business process support as necessary and required by the 
Department to transition and assume contract requirements to the Department or another Department agent should that be required during or at the end of the Contract. 
 The Contractor shall manage and maintain the appropriate number of staff to meet all requirements listed in the RFP during the transition. All reporting and record requirements, security standards, and performance 
standards are still in effect during the transition period.  
 
 4.7 Payment

entered into pursuant to this RFP by the Department shall be made in accordance with Article XI -A of the New

 Preferred Method:  Email a .pdf copy of your invoice to Helen Hayes Hospital  at:  AP@helenhayeshosp.org  
 Subject: Vendor Name - Contract Number C042654 – Billing Month  
 
 
Payment for invoices and/or vouchers submitted by the CONTRACTOR shall only be rendered electronically unless payment by paper check is expressly authorized by the Commissioner, in the Commissioner's sole discretion, due to extenuating circumstances. Such electronic payment shall be made in accordance with ordinary State procedures and practices. The CONTRACTOR shall comply with the State Comptroller's 
procedures to authorize electronic payments. Authorization forms are available at the State Comptroller's

 Prior to the start of work under the Contract, the Contractor shall procure, at its sole cost and expense, and shall maintain in force at all times during the term of the Contract, insurance of the types and in the amounts

4.10 Minority & Women- Owned Business Enterprise (M/WBE)  Requirements  
 
Pursuant to New York State Executive Law Article 15- A, the Department recognizes its obligation to promote 
opportunities for maximum feasible participation of certified  minority -and woman- owned business enterprises 
and the employment of minority group members and women in the performance of the Department’s  contracts.  
 
Business Participation Opportunities for M/WBEs  
 
For purposes of this RFP, the Department  hereby establishes an overall goal of 0 % for M/WBE participation, 
0% for Minority -Owned Business Enterprises (“MBE s”) participation and 0 % for Women- Owned Business 
Enterprises (“WBE s”), based on the current availability of qualified MBEs and WBEs and outreach efforts to 
certified M/WBE firms. The successful Bidder who becomes the Contractor under the Contract entered into

by M/WBEs as subcontractors or suppliers in the performance of the Contract consistent with the M/WBE 
participation goals established for this procurement, and Contractor must agree that the Department  may 
withhold payment pending receipt of the required M/WBE documentation. For guidance on how the 
Department  will determine “good faith efforts,” refer to 5 NYCRR §142.8.

The Contractor will be required to attempt to utilize, in good faith, any MBE or WBE identified in its M/WBE 
Utilization Plan, during the performance of the Contract. Requests for a partial or total waiver of established 
goal requirements made subsequent to Contract Award may be made at any time during the term of the Contract to the Department  but must be made no later than prior to the submission of a request for final 
payment on the Contract.  
 
  
The Contractor will be required to submit a Contractor’s Quarterly M/WBE Contractor Compliance & Payment 
Report to the Department , by the 10th day following each end of quarter over the term of the Contract 
documenting the progress made toward achievement of the M/WBE goals of the Contract.   
  
If (a) the Department determines that the Contractor is not in compliance with the M/WBE requirements of the

during future Vendor Responsibility Profile reviews should the B idder bid on future opportunities with the 
Department  
  
Such liquidated damages shall be calculated as an amount equaling the difference between: (1) all sums 
identified for payment to M/WBEs had the Contractor achieved the contractual M/WBE goals; and (2) all sums actually paid to M/WBEs for work performed or materials supplied under the Contract.    
 
  
A New York State certified Minority - and Women- Owned Businesses (M/WBE) may request that their firm’s 
contact information be included on a list of M/WBE firms interested in serving as a subcontractor for this 
procurement. The listing will be publicly posted on the Department’s website for reference by the bidding 
community. A firm requesting inclusion on this list should send contact information and a copy of its NYS 
M/WBE certification to HHHbidrequest@helenhayeshosp.org before the Deadline for Questions as specified in 
Section 1.  (Calendar of Events). Nothing prohibits an M/WBE Vendor from proposing as a prime Contractor.    
  
Please Note: Failure to comply with the foregoing requirements may result in a finding of non-responsiveness, non -responsibility and/or a breach of the Contract, leading to the withholding of 
funds, suspension or termination of the Contract or such other a ctions or enforcement proceedings as 
allowed by the Contract.)  
 
 
 

14 4.11 Participation Opportunities for NYS Certified Service- Disabled Veteran -Owned Businesses  
 
Article 17 -B of the New York State Executive Law provides for more meaningful participation in public 
procurement by NYS -certified Service- Disabled Veteran- Owned Businesses (“SDVOBs”), thereby further 
integrating such businesses into New York State’s economy. The Department  recognizes the need to promote 
the employment of service- disabled veterans and to ensure that certified service- disabled veteran- owned

 In recognition of the service and sacrifices made by service- disabled veterans and in recognition of their 
economic activity in doing business in New York State, Bidders/Contractors are strongly encouraged and expected to consider SDVOBs in the fulfillment  of the requirements of the Contract.  Such participation may be 
as subcontractors or suppliers, as protégés, or in other partnering or supporting roles.   
 For purposes of this procurement, the Department  conducted a comprehensive search and determined that the 
Contract does not offer sufficient opportunities to set specific goals for participation by SDVOBs as subcontractors, service providers, and suppliers to Contractor.   Nevertheless, Bidder/Contractor  is encouraged 
to make good faith efforts to promote and assist in the participation of SDVOBs on the Contract for the 
provision of services and materials.  The directory of New York State Certified SDVOBs can be viewed at: 
https://ogs.ny.gov/veterans/   
 Bidders are encouraged to contact the Office of General Services’ Division of Service- Disabled Veteran’s 
Business Development at 518- 474-2015 or VeteransDevelopment@ogs.ny.gov  to discuss methods of 
maximizing participation by SDVOBs on the Contract.

grants.title: Asset Verification Services
grants.summary: This grant funds the implementation of an electronic system for verifying disclosed and undisclosed assets to determine Medicaid eligibility for specific populations.
grants.description: The New York State Department of Health is seeking proposals to implement an electronic asset verification system as required by Section 1940 of the Social Security Act. This system will assist in determining and re-determining Medicaid eligibility for aged, certified blind, and certified disabled applicants and recipients. The grant aims to ensure compliance with federal requirements and improve the efficiency of Medicaid eligibility processes. Interested applicants must submit proposals by the specified deadline and meet the outlined qualifications.
grants.eligibility_notes: Eligible applicants include qualified organizations capable of implementing an electronic asset verification system for Medicaid eligibility purposes.
key_requirements: Must be a qualified organization capable of implementing an electronic asset verification system.
Must comply with Section 1940 of the Social Security Act.
Must submit proposals by February 17, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. ET.

2.0 OVERVIEW   
 
Through this Request for Proposals (“RFP”), the New York State (“State”) Department of Health (the 
“Department” or “DOH”) is seeking competitive proposals from qualified bidders to provide the  
products/services as further detailed in Section 4.0  (Scope of Work).  It is the Department’s intent to award one

2.1 Introductory Background  
 
Section 1940 of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. § 1396w) requires all states to implement an electronic system 
for verifying disclosed and undisclosed assets for purposes of determining and re -determining Medicaid eligibility 
for aged (age 65 or over), certified blind and certified disabled applicants and recipients, referred to as the SSI -
related population. “SSI” refers to the federal Supplemental Security Income program.  The New York State 
Department of Health’s (Department) Office of Health Insuranc e Programs (OHIP), Division of Eligibility and 
Marketplace Integration (DEMI) is soliciting proposals for the implementation and operation of a web -based 
Asset Verification System (AVS) for the New York State Medicaid program. The AVS will identify assets held at 
various financial institutions and conduct searches for real property owned by selected Medicaid appli cants and 
recipients and/or their spouses.    
 
By procuring the services of a contractor, the Department of Health will:  
• Provide for enrollment integrity by verifying the assets and real property of the population applying for or 
receiving Medicaid in accordance with federal requirements;  
• Provide flexibility, security, and automation that allows the Department of Health to manage and act upon 
verification results in a timely manner; and  
• Reduce fraud and abuse.  
 
New York State’s Medicaid Program  
The Department is the State’s single state agency charged with overseeing New York’s Medicaid program.  New 
York’s Medicaid program is the State’s largest payer of health care and long -term care.  Each month, more than 
six (6) million Medicaid enrollees re ceive services through a network of more than 60,000 health care providers 
and more than 16 managed care plans.   
 

4  
 
 
The Office of Health Insurance Programs, Division of Eligibility and Marketplace Integration  
The Department’s mission is to ensure high quality health services are available to New York residents.  
Consistent with this mission, the Department assures comprehensive health care and long -term care coverage 
for low and middle -income individuals and fa milies through Medicaid, Child Health Plus (CHP), and the Elderly 
Pharmaceutical Insurance Coverage (EPIC) programs. These programs are operated through OHIP, which 
oversees the administration of New York’s Medicaid program, among other responsibilities.  DEMI is the office 
within OHIP that is responsible for the establishment and implementation of eligibility and enrollment policies 
and operations for Medicaid and other programs.  DEMI also oversees Medicaid administration by State 
agencies and 58 local de partments of social services (LDSS) located in each county of the state. In New York 
City, the LDSS is the Human Resources Administration (HRA), comprised of the five (5) boroughs of Manhattan, 
Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, and Staten Island.   
 
Medicaid Applications  
For certain Medicaid categories, including the SSI -related population, applications are made through the LDSS, 
which processes the applications and subsequent renewals of Medicaid enrollees. A subset of applications and 
redeterminations will be processed through the new eligibility system, Medicaid Eligibility and Client Management 
System (MECM). Medicaid applications are processed to assess eligibility under program rules, and eligible 
individuals are subject to annual renewals to demonstrate continued eli gibility.  The Asset Verification System is 
used to obtain resource information for both the applicant and the applicant’s spouse at initial application and 
redetermination.  An eligibility determination must be made within 45 days from the date of initial application.    
 
Current New York State Medicaid Eligibility Data Systems  
The Department utilizes a data system called the Welfare Management System (WMS) to house Medicaid 
eligibility information for the SSI -related population. Information from WMS is transmitted to the State’s 
Medicaid Management Information System (MMIS).  WMS consists of two (2) mainframes – a downstate 
system for the New York City HRA, and an upstate system for the rest of the state.  Both the upstate and 
downstate WMS mainframes are computerized data systems that rec eive, maintain, and process information 
for Medicaid eligibility purposes. New York City HRA uses an additional system, Eligibility Data Image and 
Transfer System (EDITS), to receive and process Medicaid applications before transmitting the information to 
the downstate WMS.  The LDSSs have terminals linked to the mainframe and new eligibility data is entered in 
WMS by data entry unit staff and updated by nightly batches.   The Department also utilizes a new eligibility 
system in which receives information from the consumer and processes Medicaid applications and maintains 
the information.  
 
Asset and real property verification requests sent to the AVS are generated from each mainframe and 
submitted through end -of-day batch files. Data results for each request in the form of financial institution 
records, deeds, and various other asset verific ation records are posted electronically in the AVS portal for 
review and storage. The AVS portal is a web -based portal maintained by the Contractor and is housed outside 
of the WMS and MECM systems. In addition to the results returned to the portal, the De partment  also require s 
that data results for Downstate cases be sent to the Downstate EDITS System via batch file for review and 
storage within its system. AVS data responses are also to be returned to the MECM system. The Department  
require s the selected Contractor to return AVS responses to the AVS portal, the Downstate EDITS System and  
the MECM system.

2. Asset Verification System  
 
The Department requires the selected Contractor to provide  an Asset Verification system which will search for 
and verif y assets and real property that are owned by Medicaid applicants and recipients and/or their spouses. 
The Asset Verification System shall electronically verify accounts held in financial institutions, and conduct 
searches on real property, owned by the appl icant or recipient and/or the applicant/recipient’s spouse for the 
month of application and a three -(3) month retroactive period.  For i ndividuals applying for Medicaid coverage of 
nursing home care, the verification system will:  
 
• Verify the individual’s and the spouse’s accounts held in financial institutions for the month of application 
and the 60 -month look back period, and the month(s) between the application date and the request date, 
including accounts that were closed during this period.  The information should include the account balance 
as of the first minute of the first day of the month, average daily balance, and interest earned for each 
month of the look -back period;  
• Identify months in which a potential transfer of assets is detected as determined based on criteria approved 
by the State; and  
• Conduct searches on real property owned by the individual or the individual’s spouse during the month of 
application and the 60 -month look -back period, including any real property that was sold or transferred 
during this period.   
 
The Contractor will be able to conduct Asset Verification searches for other individuals as established by the 
Department for a look -back period to be determined by the Department but not to exceed 60 -months prior to the 
date of application.  
 
The Contractor will utilize one (1) integrated system to find/verify both assets and real property . This solution will 
utilize secure web -based techniques to identify assets and real property that might otherwise not be discovered 
or are not disclosed through the Medicaid application or recertification process. The Contractor is expected to 
process all asset and property verification requests and deliver the search results within ten (10) calendar days 
from the date of the request.
